arxiv-2112-00015.title: To be or not to be a black hole: detailed binary population models as a sanity check 2021 To be or not to be a black hole: detailed binary population models as a sanity check – References
arxiv-2112-00015.creator: H. F. Stevance, S. G. Parsons J. J. Eldridge
arxiv-2112-00015.description: Abstract We use the self-consistent stellar populations in the Binary Population A Spectral Synthesis (BPASS) models to assess whether NGC1850-BH1 is a black hole. Using search criteria based on reported physical properties in the literature we purposefully search for suitable systems with a black hole (or compact object) companion: we do not find any.

arxiv-2202-06466.title: Measuring “Why” in Recommender Systems: a Comprehensive Survey on the Evaluation of Explainable Recommendation
arxiv-2202-06466.creator: Xu Chen, Yongfeng Zhang, Ji-Rong Wen
arxiv-2202-06466.description: Abstract Explainable recommendation has shown its great advantages for improving recommendation persuasiveness, user satisfaction, system transparency and among others. A fundamental problem of explainable recommendation is how to evaluate the explanations. In the past few years, various evaluation strategies have been proposed. However, they are scattered in different papers, and there lacks a systematic and detailed comparison between them.

arxiv-2208-05560.title: Theory review for hadronic corrections to 𝒈 − 𝟐 g-2
arxiv-2208-05560.creator: Maarten Golterman
arxiv-2208-05560.description: Abstract We review Standard-Model evaluations of hadronic contributions to the muon anomalous magnetic moment g − 2 g-2 . Most space is devoted to the hadronic vacuum polarization contribution, in view of the discrepancy between the data-based dispersive evaluation and the lattice evaluation by the BMW collaboration.

arxiv-2209-12301.title: Constant-delay enumeration for SLP-compressed documents
arxiv-2209-12301.creator: Martín Muñoz ORCID:0009-0003-3294-6159, Cristian Riveros ORCID:0000-0003-0832-116X
arxiv-2209-12301.description: Abstract . We study the problem of enumerating results from a query over a compressed document. The model we use for compression are straight-line programs (SLPs), which are defined by a context-free grammar that produces a single string. For our queries, we use a model called Annotated Automata, an extension of regular automata that allows annotations on letters.

arxiv-2307-04877.title: Engineering bound states in continuum via nonlinearity induced extra dimension
arxiv-2307-04877.creator: Qingtian Miao, Jayakrishnan M. P. Nair, Girish S. Agarwal
arxiv-2307-04877.description: Abstract Bound states in continuum (BICs) are localized states of a system possessing significantly large life times with applications across various branches of science. In this work, we propose an expedient protocol to engineer BICs which involves the use of Kerr nonlinearities in the system.

arxiv-2405-02001.title: On finding optimal collective variables for complex systems by minimizing the deviation between effective and full dynamics
arxiv-2405-02001.creator: Wei Zhang, Christof Schütte
arxiv-2405-02001.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Wei Zhang, Christof Schütte. This paper is concerned with collective variables, or reaction coordinates, that map a discrete-in-time Markov process X n X_{n} in ℝ d \mathbb{R}^{d} to a (much) smaller dimension k ≪ d k\ll d . We define the effective dynamics under a given collective variable map ξ \xi as the best Markovian representation of X n X_{n} under ξ \xi .

arxiv-2412-05127.title: The Prompt Canvas: A Literature-Based Practitioner Guide for Creating Effective Prompts in Large Language Models
arxiv-2412-05127.creator: Michael Hewing, Vincent Leinhos
arxiv-2412-05127.description: Abstract The rise of large language models (LLMs) has highlighted the importance of prompt engineering as a crucial technique for optimizing model outputs. While experimentation with various prompting methods, such as Few-shot, Chain-of-Thought, and role-based techniques, has yielded promising results, these advancements remain fragmented across academic papers, blog posts and anecdotal experimentation.

arxiv-2502-01198.title: Scalable, nanoscale positioning of highly coherent color centers in prefabricated diamond nanostructures
arxiv-2502-01198.creator: Sunghoon Kim, Paz London, Daipeng Yang, Lillian B. Hughes, Jeffrey Ahlers, Simon Meynell, William J. Mitchell, Kunal Mukherjee, Ania C. Bleszynski Jayich
arxiv-2502-01198.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Sunghoon Kim, Paz London, Daipeng Yang, Lillian B. Hughes, Jeffrey Ahlers, Simon Meynell, William J. Mitchell, Kunal Mukherjee, Ania C. Bleszynski Jayich. Nanophotonic devices in color center-containing hosts provide efficient readout, control, and entanglement of the embedded emitters. Yet control over color center formation – in number, position, and coherence – in nanophotonic devices remains a challenge to scalability. Here, we report a controlled creation of highly coherent diamond nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers with nanoscale three-dimensional localization in prefabricated nanostructures with high yield.

arxiv-2509-15541.title: Stress Testing Deliberative Alignment for Anti-Scheming Training
arxiv-2509-15541.creator: Bronson Schoen, Evgenia Nitishinskaya, Mikita Balesni, Axel Højmark, Angela Fan, Andrei Matveiakin, Rusheb Shah, Marcus Williams, Amelia Glaese, Boaz Barak, Wojciech Zaremba, Marius Hobbhahn, Apollo Research & OpenAI
arxiv-2509-15541.description: Abstract Highly capable AI systems could secretly pursue misaligned goals – what we call “scheming”. Because a scheming AI would deliberately try to hide its misaligned goals and actions, measuring and mitigating scheming requires different strategies than are typically used in ML.

arxiv-2510-05872.title: Entanglement dynamics and performance of two-qubit gates for superconducting qubits under non-Markovian effects
arxiv-2510-05872.creator: Kiyoto Nakamura, Joachim Ankerhold
arxiv-2510-05872.description: Abstract Within a numerically exact simulation technique, the dissipative dynamics of a two-qubit architecture is considered in which each qubit couples to its individual noise source (reservoir). The goal is to reveal the role of subtle qubit–reservoir correlations including non-Markovian processes as a prerequisite to guide further improvements of quantum computing devices. This paper addresses the following three topics.

pmc-10572390.creator: Silvia Cristina Da Costa Dutra, Xavier Oriol Granado, Darío Paéz-Rovira, Virginia Díaz, Claudia Carrasco-Dajer, Alicia Izquierdo
pmc-10572390.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). One of the greatest challenges in the domain of emotional regulation is comprehending the functionality of strategies and their utilization in various social contexts. In this sense, this study analyzes differences in the use and efficacy of regulation strategies, particularly of interpersonal strategies like altruism, social support, negotiation, mediation, regulation, and rituals, in samples of workers (N = 687) and students (N = 959) from Brazil, Chile, Cuba, Spain, and Uruguay, and athletes (N =144) from Spain.

pmc-11688012.title: Saliva and serum biomarkers in oral diseases: A case–control study
pmc-11688012.creator: Aliaa Al Shaar, Omar Hamadeh, Ayman Ali
pmc-11688012.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Saliva stands out as an advantageous diagnostic fluid due to various reasons that make it a reliable and practical source for analysis. Its abundance facilitates easy and large-scale sample collection, enhancing its diagnostic utility. The simplicity of collecting and storing saliva samples, combined with its accessibility and cost-effectiveness compared to other body fluids, makes it an attractive choice for diagnostic purposes.

uslaw-usc-t10-s2200d.description: United States Code, Title 10 (Armed Forces); Part III (Training And Education); Chapter 112 (Cyber Scholarship Program). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. The Secretary of Defense shall prescribe regulations for the administration of this chapter.
